svg.title: What setup-agent-ready-codebase does, in three steps
svg.desc: The problem: an agent can read your code and write tests, but many codebases lack a setup that lets it check a change reliably. Parallel work breaks, checks need a person, and a passing test can mean little. The fix: you run one command, and the skill learns what your project is and what it needs, asks which tools you want and how strict the checks should be, adds only what is missing, and looks again until nothing is left to add. It checks twelve areas: tools, parallel work, linting, tests, sign-in, flow or component tests, browser use, logging, pull request proof, lessons, test review and instructions file. The result: an agent can change code, run checks, capture proof and open a pull request, guided by a short instructions file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) that points to one guide per topic.

svg.text: Now an agent can change code and prove it works
Every check is a command with the same verdict on every run, and a short file tells the agent which to run.
Works in its own copy of the project, with its own ports.
Lint for each file type, unit and integration tests, and e2e or component tests.
A screenshot per step, and a video for live interactions, annotated for review.
With the proof attached, so a reviewer can see it working.
Your AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. It tells an agent how things work
here, and which guide to read for which task, so it loads only
